statement.text:
For a group G, let Dn (G) denote the n-th dimension subgroup of G,
and ζn (G) the n-th term of its upper central series. For a given integer n ⩾ 1,
let f (n) = max{m | ∃ a nilpotent group G of class n with Dm (G) ̸= 1} and
g(n) = max{m | ∃ a nilpotent group G of class n such that Dn (G) ̸⊆ ζm (G)}.
    a) What is f (3)?
    b) (B. I. Plotkin). Is it true that f (n) is finite for all n?
    c) Is the growth of f (n) and g(n) polynomial, exponential, or intermediary?
    It is known that both f (n) − n and g(n) tend to infinity as n → ∞ (N. Gupta,
Yu. V. Kuz’min, J. Pure Appl. Algebra, 104 (1995), 191–197).
                                                                R. Mikhailov, I. B. S. Passi
